result.topic_en: Concluding table of the coefficients N and M for large ratios n of pipe length to diameter, with the rule that for n > 50000 one has N = 4000/n and M = 30 ft, and a discussion of how friction reduces the height of a fountain jet.

DE FRICTIONE FLVIDORVM. 385

113. Non opus eſt, vt haec tabula vlterius continuetur; ſi enim fuerit $n$ numerus maior, quam 50000, erit iuſte $N = \frac{4000}{n}$, et $M = 30$ ped. Quaecunque ergo fuerit diſtantia, ſeu longitudo, canalis, eiusque diameter, ex quoto $n$, qui ex diuiſione longitudinis per diametrum reſultat, ope huius tabulae facile excerpuntur valores N et M, quibus inuentis, ſi eleuatio aquae in caſtello ſupra fontem ponatur $= q$, erit altitudo fontis $v = Nq - M$ ped.

114. Si nulla eſſet frictio, altitudo fontis $v$ aequalis eſſet altitudini caſtelli $q$, ſeu $v = q$. Vnde patet, ob frictionem hanc altitudinem $q$ duplici modo diminui: primum enim multiplicari debet per N, qui eſt numerus vnitate minor; tum vero inſuper ab hoc producto ſubtrahi debet altitudo M, quae 30 pedes ſuperare nequit, atque haec poſtrema diminutio preſſioni
Tom. VI. Nou. Com. Ccc atmoſ-

items.quote: ſi enim fuerit $n$ numerus maior, quam 50000, erit iuſte $N = \frac{4000}{n}$, et $M = 30$ ped.
items.english: For if n is a number greater than 50000, then exactly N = 4000/n and M = 30 ft.

items.quote: ſi eleuatio aquae in caſtello ſupra fontem ponatur $= q$, erit altitudo fontis $v = Nq - M$ ped.
items.english: If the elevation of the water in the reservoir above the fountain is set = q, the height of the fountain will be v = Nq − M ft.

items.quote: tum vero inſuper ab hoc producto ſubtrahi debet altitudo M, quae 30 pedes ſuperare nequit
items.english: and then moreover from this product must be subtracted the height M, which cannot exceed 30 feet
